california.deadline_description: Landlord must furnish an itemized statement and refund within 21 calendar days after tenant vacates.
california.forfeiture_rule: Failure to provide itemized statement within 21 days forfeits landlord's right to retain any portion of security deposit (Granberry v. Islay Investments).
california.bad_faith_penalty_rule: Statutory damages up to twice the amount of the security deposit for bad-faith withholding under § 1950.5(l).
allowable_deductions: Unpaid rent owed under valid agreement
Cleaning necessary to return unit to initial move-in level of cleanliness
Repair of damages exceeding normal wear and tear caused by tenant or guests
prohibited_deductions: Ordinary wear and tear resulting from normal residential use
Repainting walls where tenancy exceeded 2 years unless unauthorized damage occurred
Routine carpet cleaning or carpet replacement without documented tenant-caused destruction
Pre-existing damages documented prior to tenancy
Charges for landlord's personal time without actual third-party vendor receipts

new_york.statute_title: New York General Obligations Law Section 7-108
new_york.deadline_description: Landlord must provide an itemized statement and return deposit within 14 days after tenant vacates.
new_york.forfeiture_rule: If landlord fails to provide itemized statement within 14 days, landlord forfeits any right to retain any portion of the deposit under Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act (HSTPA).
new_york.bad_faith_penalty_rule: Punitive damages up to double the deposit amount for willful violation under § 7-108(1-a)(g).
allowable_deductions: Unpaid rent accrued during lawful occupancy
Damage caused by tenant beyond normal wear and tear
Non-utility charges authorized explicitly by signed lease
prohibited_deductions: Normal wear and tear from customary usage
Painting or wall maintenance required by local housing maintenance codes
Wear to floors, appliances, and fixtures consistent with age and occupancy
Deductions made without attaching detailed itemized repair receipts

painting.statutory_standard: Under state guidelines, residential interior paint has a 2-year useful life. After 2 years of occupancy, repainting is 100% normal wear-and-tear.

carpet.statutory_standard: Carpet has a standard 5-year useful life. Routine cleaning fees upon vacancy cannot be deducted if tenant maintained reasonable broom-clean cleanliness.

cleaning.statutory_standard: Landlords cannot deduct for standard turnover cleaning. Deductions are lawful only to restore the unit to its move-in cleanliness level.

hardware_and_fixtures.statutory_standard: Minor picture-hanging nail holes, pin holes, and minor hardware loosening constitute ordinary residential wear and tear.
